observation: Domestic (KUNA) and foreign (KUNX) customers are defined relative to the selling company's country: 0 of 1267 KUNA/KUNX lines contradict it.
why_it_is_normal: KNA1 has no company code, so a customer in GB or US is domestic for company 3000 or 2000. Compared against T001.LAND1 the account groups are consistent.

observation: 7 lines have a baseline date before the document date; all are in type AB (reversals).
why_it_is_normal: A reversal inherits the baseline date of the document it cancels. Both are excluded from the metrics (see the reversal entry).

observation: 484 lines have an abbreviated code as text (cogs, mkt, it, rent, cons, trav, off, util); 3857 lines have no text.
why_it_is_normal: SGTXT is free text with no defined format in the README, and the type of expense comes from the G/L account (HKONT), so nothing depends on it.

observation: Every document balances: debits equal credits in local currency; 0 documents do not.
why_it_is_normal: This confirms that SHKZG and DMBTR are consistent with each other.

observation: The largest document amount outside the opening balances is 76,784.33; the amounts above 200,000 are all in the opening-balance documents.
why_it_is_normal: No amount outliers in the year's activity.

observation: 167 customer/vendor lines have no clearing document at the end of the year (111 customer: 89 invoices and 22 credit memos; 56 vendor); the latest clearing date in the data is 2025-12-31, so none was cleared after the key date.
why_it_is_normal: An empty clearing document (AUGBL) is how SAP marks an open item; it is not an error. It is the definition of the open items (receivables and payables) at the key date, so it is stated here as an assumption. The open credit memos have their own entry in the log.
